To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gut microbiome is a major determinant of the immune system, which can lead to a number of human diseases.
the microbiome is a key player in the development of the immune system and in the pathogenesis of inflammatory and metabolic disorders.
the microbiome is a major regulator of the human immune system and that microbial metabolites play critical roles in this process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of the microbiome and the metabolites it produces in the development and maintenance of human health.
understanding the mechanisms by which microbial metabolites influence human health and disease.
understanding how the gut microbiome shapes the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gut microbiota is essential for human physiology and that its disruption can result in disease, and that it can be manipulated to prevent or ameliorate disease.
the microbiota is a key regulator of human health.
the microbiome has a profound influence on human health, and the gut microbiome is a critical regulator of the immune response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gut microbiota is a critical regulator of the immune system and that microbial metabolites play a central role in shaping the immune system.

the microbiome plays an important role in the regulation of the host's metabolism, and that this role is mediated by the gut microbiome's metabolites, which can affect the development and function of the host's immune system.
the human gut microbiome is a critical regulator of the host’s immune system and is an emerging target for the prevention and treatment of human inflammatory and metabolic disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the microbiome is a critical determinant of host health, and that the microbiome should be considered as part of the host holobiont, a term coined in the 1960s to describe the symbiotic relationship between an organism and its microbial community.
the gut microbiota is a critical component of the immune system and that its dysregulation has profound effects on human health and disease.
the microbiome can be manipulated to treat disease and that this manipulation can be achieved by targeting the microbiome directly or by modulating the host metabolism to influence the microbiota.
